title: Is this a good UI for an anime styled idle game?
author: AIGameCoder
selftext: I don't know if the pixel text really fits well with the art aesthetics, but I also want to keep the UI simple.

comments.author: angrylittledev
comments.body: Not really it clashes pixel text with 2D flat cell shaded anime style, if you like the art then keep everything in that style. Those pixels are the first thing user sees.

replies.author: AIGameCoder
replies.body: Yeah I'm switching to a more modern font to match the cell shaded style

comments.author: AutomaticTalent
comments.body:
I found that playing my game and making interface tweaks along the way worked great. 

Once I got into the game the needs of the interface developed alongside the look.

comments.author: Ambitious-Crew-7132
comments.body: a lot inconsistencies, also my small advice would be work little more with AI visuals, this is just little too "chatgpt prompt result done" rather than thoughtful designs and style, but i understand it's probably early stages

replies.author: AIGameCoder
replies.body: Any specific inconsistencies come to mind? Consistent art is such a huge problem with AI image generation, so that's a huge workflow I want to improve before generating new assets.

replies.author: Omega0Alpha
replies.body:
Find inspiration from other games online, or let chatgpt give you only a text description of what the gamme is about and how it should be played (it should not mention the UI style it used here)  
Then create a new chat and tell it to visualize how the ui for this game \[using the text prompt about the game\] would look like

replies.author: Ambitious-Crew-7132
replies.body:
If I were to say my first impression, the bottom part feels pretty unfitting compared to the left, right, and middle sections. The buttons look sort of empty, and the font feels awkward. I'd redesign everything at the bottom so it doesn't have so much empty space.

I also don't like the background in the middle scene. It's very detailed for no particular reason, usually you wanna blur it out a little, and the characters don't fit it that well. Overall, I don't really see a strong vibe there, it lacks "wow" effect, something that makes the game feel like *your* game, something unique and distinctive. 

I'd recommend looking at retro games for inspirations.

replies.author: AethericPulse
replies.body:
I ran into similar issues, what works at times is to use AI to create individual assets so you can adjust as needed without having key aspects vary constantly.
What I found out is the heavier an image is on variety of images, the more AI deviate. 
Example of what I meant before is for my titlescreen, the logo, buttons and a particular npc are separate pngs that are added to the main image. 
AI couldn't put in the no even when given as a png.

comments.author: AethericPulse
comments.body: Big tip when you feel unsure, just paste in your UI into AI and ask for a thorough review of the UI along with recommendations for edits and why

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: your character visuals are pretty much mobile game-esque, you may as well match them with a mobile game UI

comments.author: AgitatedUse4032
comments.body: I love all the characters lined up like that, reminds me of mu online character selection screen. They would look awesome with wings and some basic movement on their spot like small weapon movements or particles effects.

replies.author: AIGameCoder
replies.body: Particle effects are a great idea. This is for a jame gam so the game is already fully functional, so its perfect to implement special effects.
